issues.where: frames 666 to 680, the whole stage around the globe
issues.what: The wooden icicle base, the snowflake doily, the blue bokeh and the bare floor all turn into the moss base, pink bokeh and petal-strewn floor within about 14 frames. The camera is still and the base is in full view, with the globe lifted off to the right. Nothing hides it, so at normal speed it reads as the whole room being swapped.
issues.fix: Hide the swap. Cover the base with storm and lift so it is never seen, or grow the stage over 1 to 2 s after the landing, starting with the bokeh and floor and then growing moss over the base. Do not hard-swap everything in one window.

issues.what: This clean frame is half one season and half another. The storm inside the globe is already pink spring while the base, the doily, the floor and the blue bokeh are still winter.
issues.fix: Tie the storm's colour to the stage change so they move together, or keep the storm white until the stage starts to turn.

issues.what: The globe only slides left, right and up. The base stays level in every frame, so there is no tilt, let alone one that lags, and the shake reads as a mechanical translation rather than a heavy thing held in a hand.
issues.fix: Add a roll of 6 to 12 degrees that trails each stroke by a few frames and overshoots at the reversals. Make the lift tip the globe slightly toward the hand.

issues.where: frames 628 to 718 and on into set-B-01 at 720
issues.what: The storm fills the globe as a uniform opaque milky white, then pink, for about 1.5 s. It reads as frosted glass or fog rather than many particles in liquid, and the lag, slam and fold cannot be seen inside the opaque mass.
issues.fix: Cut the storm's opacity so the scene and darker gaps show through. Use clear streaks of particles at several depths, with a visible fold and whirl, rather than a flat fill.

issues.where: the arrival as a whole, 720 to 898 across set-B-01 to set-B-08
issues.what: The new season does not grow in. The pink fog dissolves to reveal a tree already in full blossom, a finished lawn and a finished house. Only the fog changes, so the arrival is a reveal or wipe rather than growth.
issues.fix: Grow the season under the clearing. Let the blossom open and fill the canopy, the grass rise and the flowers bloom over the 3 s of clearing, so growth is still visible once the fog is thin.

issues.where: the left side of the moss base, from 738 on, growing through set-B-04 to set-B-08
issues.what: A white waterfall emitter and its stream appear on the base and lengthen in full view during the arrival, so the base visibly changes after the landing.
issues.fix: Either have the waterfall present from the moment the base is revealed, or grow it in an obviously organic way, with water running from the top and a splash at the floor, so it does not read as an asset popping in.

issues.what: The camera push-in at rest cuts the top of the globe off the frame for about 3 s. The pull-back from 1138 to 1190 is also the fastest part of the move, so it lands abruptly rather than with weight.
issues.fix: Stop the push before the crown leaves frame, keeping at least a 5% margin above the glass. Ease the pull-back with a longer ease-in and ease-out so its peak speed is no higher than the push-in's.

issues.where: the floor petals beside the base, 722 to 742
issues.what: A ring of large petals bursts out around the base about 30 frames after the landing at about 692. The surface answers the set down late rather than on impact.
issues.fix: Fire the floor-petal scatter on the landing frame, with a small first burst and settling after it.

issues.what: About 10 s after the landing the petal density looks almost unchanged, and few petals are seen settling on the lawn or the roof. The fall does not visibly die away.
issues.fix: Thin the airborne petals over time, and let more of them come to rest and pile on the grass, the roof and the tree.
